question:
A 1.5 cm simple, unilocular pancreatic cyst is incidentally discovered on a CT scan in a 54-year-old
patient with no history of pancreatic disease. What is the MOST appropriate recommendation? Answer
Choices: (A) Antibiotic therapy for presumed infection (B) Endoscopic ultrasound with fine-needle
aspiration (C) Observation without further imaging (D) Serum CA 19-9 level measurement (E) MRCP
(F) Referral to oncology for evaluation (G) Repeat CT in 1 year (H) Immediate biopsy of the pancreatic

cyst (I) Surgical resection (J) PET scan to rule out malignancy
 A. Observation without further imaging
B. Repeat CT in 1 year
C. PET scan to rule out malignancy
D. Antibiotic therapy for presumed infection
E. MRCP
F. Surgical resection
G. Endoscopic ultrasound with fine-needle aspiration
H. Immediate biopsy of the pancreatic cyst
I. Referral to oncology for evaluation
J. Serum CA 19-9 level measurement
